skill.name: clinicaltrials-database
skill.description: Search ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 by condition, intervention, location, status, sponsor, phase, or NCT ID, then summarize or export public trial data.
skill.summary: Search, inspect, summarize, and export public ClinicalTrials.gov study records.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The audit reviewed 114 static findings and found the flagged network, filesystem, reconnaissance, and command patterns consistent with the declared research workflow. Network calls use the official ClinicalTrials.gov endpoint, CSV writes are explicit examples, and backticks are Markdown formatting. Two availability risks remain: executable requests lack timeouts, and bulk pagination has no default request cap.

remediation.issue: Executable HTTP requests can wait indefinitely.
remediation.suggestion: Set explicit connect and read timeouts on every request, then surface timeout errors clearly.

remediation.issue: Bulk retrieval has no default page or request limit.
remediation.suggestion: Set conservative page and result caps, honor rate limits, and require explicit confirmation before uncapped retrieval.

semantic_findings.title: Network Requests Lack Timeouts
semantic_findings.description: Executable requests omit timeouts, so an unresponsive service can hold the agent process indefinitely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both executable requests omit a timeout argument. The later documentation recommends a timeout, confirming the helper implementation gap.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Pagination Has No Default Request Cap
semantic_findings.description: Bulk search defaults to no result cap and requests maximum-size pages until pagination ends. Broad searches can consume excessive memory, time, and API quota.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The function defaults max_results to None and loops until no page token remains. Each request asks for 1,000 records without delay or a page cap.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant public trial records requires precise filters and careful review of nested registry data. This skill searches ClinicalTrials.gov and produces focused summaries or exports.
actual_capabilities: Search public studies by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, recruitment status, phase, or NCT ID.
Retrieve detailed registry information for a specific NCT ID.
Paginate through matching studies and apply a caller-provided result limit.
Return ClinicalTrials.gov responses in JSON or CSV format.
Extract concise study summaries with status, phase, enrollment, description, and update date.
Show common query, error handling, pagination, and CSV export patterns.
limitations: The skill requires internet access and depends on ClinicalTrials.gov availability and rate limits.
Registry data is sponsor-submitted and may be incomplete, delayed, or changed after retrieval.
The skill does not provide medical advice or make final eligibility decisions.
Broad bulk searches can consume significant time and memory unless result limits are set.

use_cases.title: Find Research Cohorts
use_cases.description: Search recruiting studies by disease, intervention, location, status, and phase for a focused research review.

use_cases.title: Review Trial Options
use_cases.description: Compare public eligibility, contacts, and locations before discussing possible studies with a qualified care team.

use_cases.title: Monitor Development Portfolios
use_cases.description: Track sponsor activity, study phases, recruitment states, and result availability across an intervention area.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recruiting Trials
prompt_templates.prompt: Find up to 10 recruiting ClinicalTrials.gov studies for [condition] in [location]. List NCT ID, title, status, phase, and last update.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a focused trial search with basic condition and location filters.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve [NCT ID]. Summarize purpose, eligibility, interventions, outcomes, contacts, locations, and last update. Clearly mark missing fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the main registry sections for a known trial.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sponsor Studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Search studies sponsored by [organization] for [condition]. Compare status, phase, enrollment, interventions, start dates, and result availability in a table.
prompt_templates.scenario: Analyze an organization portfolio within a disease area.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Trial Landscape
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect up to [limit] studies for [condition] and [intervention] across [statuses]. Deduplicate NCT IDs, group by phase, identify trends, and cite each record.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a bounded, multi-filter evidence landscape for advanced analysis.

output_examples.input: Find up to 10 recruiting asthma studies in Boston.
output: Search summary: Up to 10 matching recruiting studies are listed.
Columns: NCT ID, title, phase, status, facility, city, and last update.
Source note: Each result is identified by its ClinicalTrials.gov NCT ID.

output_examples.input: Summarize NCT04852770 and focus on eligibility and contacts.
output: Trial overview: title, sponsor, recruitment status, phase, enrollment, and last update.
Eligibility review: age, sex, healthy volunteer status, and registry criteria.
Contact review: central contacts and study locations, with missing fields clearly marked.

output_examples.input: Compare completed Alzheimer disease studies with posted results.
output: Comparison table: NCT ID, title, sponsor, phase, enrollment, completion date, and result availability.
Summary: studies are grouped by phase and ordered by the most recent registry update.
Caution: registry entries require source verification before clinical or policy decisions.

best_practices: Use specific conditions and statuses, then set a result limit before broad searches.
Verify each record date and source page before making research or referral decisions.
Exclude names, contact details, and other protected health information from search terms.
anti_patterns: Do not treat registry matching as a final eligibility decision or medical recommendation.
Do not request uncapped bulk results when a focused query can answer the question.
Do not interpret missing registry fields as proof that information does not exist.

faq.question: Does this skill require a ClinicalTrials.gov API key?
faq.answer: No. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: Can it find trials near a patient?
faq.answer: It can filter public study locations. Confirm current recruitment and site details directly with the listed study contact.

faq.question: Can it determine whether someone qualifies?
faq.answer: No. It can summarize registry criteria, but the study team makes the final eligibility decision.

faq.question: Which response formats are supported?
faq.answer: The API supports JSON and CSV. The helper returns parsed JSON data or CSV text.

faq.question: How current are the results?
faq.answer: Results reflect the latest available registry response. Review each record last-update date because sponsors control submissions.

faq.question: How should large searches be handled?
faq.answer: Use narrow filters, explicit result limits, maximum page sizes, and rate-aware delays. Avoid unbounded retrieval.
